_RelationDirections.summary: Direction of a relationship relative to the annotated field.
_RelationDirections.authors: `IN` means the relationship points into this node; `OUT` means it points out from this node.
_RelationDirections.implementers: Treat as the edge direction when planning traversals for `@relationship`. Reject values other than `IN` / `OUT`.

@node.summary: Marks a GraphQL object type as a graph node. Optional `subgraph` attributes multi-source ownership; optional `labels` name the node labels in the graph store.

authors.intro: Put `@node` on object types that represent graph nodes. Queries and mutations over that type then treat it as a node (labels default to the GraphQL type name unless you set `labels`). When several Neo4j sources are composed, set `subgraph` to the same composition name used elsewhere for that source.

implementers.intro: `subgraph` is composition metadata only — it does not change graph labels. Use `labels` (or the type name) as the node’s store identity. Do not require a particular library API.
implementers.loaders: Schemas that use `@node` must `@link` this family and import the directive. Preserve apps through Supergraph composition.
implementers.runtime: Resolve the type as a node with the given labels. Ignore `subgraph` for store I/O; use it only to attribute ownership in a multi-source Supergraph.
implementers.validation: Reject unknown args. When `labels` is present it must be a list of strings. When `subgraph` is present it must be a string matching the composition subgraph name for that source.

subgraph.constraints: A subgraph name string. When set, it must be the same identifier used for that source in composition — the same name as on `@transport(subgraph:)` and elsewhere for this subgraph. Do not invent a second name for the same source.
subgraph.validation: If present, must be a non-empty string equal to the composition subgraph name for this source.
subgraph.authors: Name which composed subgraph owns this annotation. Use the same subgraph name you use everywhere else for that source. Omit when a single-source schema does not need attribution.
subgraph.implementers: Attribute the directive to that composition subgraph name. Never invent a second name for the same source. Do not send `subgraph` to the graph store.

labels.defaults: Optional; default label is the GraphQL type name.
labels.constraints: List of node label strings in the graph store.
labels.validation: If present, must be a list of strings (may be empty only if the runtime documents that case; prefer at least one label).
labels.authors: Override the default label when the store uses different label names than the GraphQL type.
labels.implementers: Use these labels for node identity and Cypher/MATCH planning. If omitted, use the GraphQL type name as the sole label.

@relationshipProperties.summary: Marks an object type as the property bag carried on a relationship (not a node).

authors.intro: Put `@relationshipProperties` on the object type that holds edge properties. Reference that type name from `@relationship(properties:)`.

implementers.runtime: Treat the type as relationship properties, not as a node. `subgraph` is composition metadata only.
implementers.validation: Reject unknown args. `subgraph`, when present, must be a string matching the composition subgraph name.

subgraph.constraints: A subgraph name string. When set, it must be the same identifier used for that source in composition — the same name as on `@transport(subgraph:)` and elsewhere for this subgraph. Do not invent a second name for the same source.
subgraph.validation: If present, must be a non-empty string equal to the composition subgraph name for this source.
subgraph.authors: Name which composed subgraph owns this annotation. Use the same subgraph name you use everywhere else for that source. Omit when a single-source schema does not need attribution.
subgraph.implementers: Attribute ownership only; do not send `subgraph` to the graph store.

@relationship.summary: Declares that a field is a graph relationship to another node type, with a relationship type name and direction.

authors.intro: Annotate fields that traverse to related nodes. `type` is the relationship type in the store; `direction` is relative to this field’s node; `properties` names an optional `@relationshipProperties` type.

implementers.runtime: Plan traversals using `type` + `direction` (+ `properties` when set). `subgraph` is composition metadata only.
implementers.validation: Require `type` for an executable relationship. `direction`, when present, must be `IN` or `OUT`. `properties`, when present, must name a type marked `@relationshipProperties`.

subgraph.constraints: A subgraph name string. When set, it must be the same identifier used for that source in composition — the same name as on `@transport(subgraph:)` and elsewhere for this subgraph. Do not invent a second name for the same source.
subgraph.validation: If present, must be a non-empty string equal to the composition subgraph name for this source.
subgraph.authors: Name which composed subgraph owns this annotation. Use the same subgraph name you use everywhere else for that source. Omit when a single-source schema does not need attribution.
subgraph.implementers: Attribute ownership only; do not send `subgraph` to the graph store.

type.constraints: Relationship type name in the graph store.
type.validation: Reject empty or missing `type` for executable apps.
type.authors: The relationship type stored on the edge.
type.implementers: Use as the relationship type in traversal planning.

direction.validation: If present, must be exactly `IN` or `OUT`.
direction.authors: Edge direction relative to this field’s node.

properties.validation: If present, must refer to a type that carries `@relationshipProperties`.
properties.authors: Attach a properties type to this relationship.
properties.implementers: Bind edge properties to that type’s fields.

@alias.summary: Maps a GraphQL field to a different property key in the graph store.

authors.intro: Use when the GraphQL field name differs from the stored property key (including after renames). Queries still use the GraphQL name; persistence uses `property`.

implementers.runtime: Read/write the store property named by `property` for this GraphQL field. `subgraph` is composition metadata only.
implementers.validation: Require non-empty `property`. `subgraph`, when present, must match the composition subgraph name.

subgraph.constraints: A subgraph name string. When set, it must be the same identifier used for that source in composition — the same name as on `@transport(subgraph:)` and elsewhere for this subgraph. Do not invent a second name for the same source.
subgraph.validation: If present, must be a non-empty string equal to the composition subgraph name for this source.
subgraph.authors: Name which composed subgraph owns this annotation. Use the same subgraph name you use everywhere else for that source. Omit when a single-source schema does not need attribution.
subgraph.implementers: Attribute ownership only; do not send `subgraph` to the graph store.

property.constraints: Property key in the graph store.
property.authors: Stored property name for this field.
property.implementers: Map GraphQL field ↔ this property key on read/write.

@cypher.summary: Resolves a field with a custom Cypher statement, taking the named return column as the field value.

authors.intro: Provide `statement` (Cypher) and `columnName` (the return alias used as the field result). `this` refers to the current node when the field is on a node type.

implementers.runtime: Run `statement` in the field’s context; take the value of `columnName` from the result as the GraphQL field value. `subgraph` is composition metadata only.
implementers.validation: Require non-empty `statement` and `columnName`. Reject unknown args.

subgraph.constraints: A subgraph name string. When set, it must be the same identifier used for that source in composition — the same name as on `@transport(subgraph:)` and elsewhere for this subgraph. Do not invent a second name for the same source.
subgraph.validation: If present, must be a non-empty string equal to the composition subgraph name for this source.
subgraph.authors: Name which composed subgraph owns this annotation. Use the same subgraph name you use everywhere else for that source. Omit when a single-source schema does not need attribution.
subgraph.implementers: Attribute ownership only; do not send `subgraph` to the graph store.

statement.authors: Query body; use `this` for the current node when applicable.
statement.implementers: Execute as the field’s Cypher body.

columnName.constraints: Return column alias from the Cypher result.
columnName.validation: Must be a non-empty string naming a returned column.
columnName.authors: Which returned column becomes the GraphQL field value.
columnName.implementers: Project that column as the field result.

@plural.summary: Overrides the plural name used for generated list/connection field names for this type.

authors.intro: Set `value` when the default pluralization of the type name is wrong (e.g. `people` instead of `persons`).

implementers.runtime: Use `value` wherever plural field names are generated for this type. `subgraph` is composition metadata only.

subgraph.constraints: A subgraph name string. When set, it must be the same identifier used for that source in composition — the same name as on `@transport(subgraph:)` and elsewhere for this subgraph. Do not invent a second name for the same source.
subgraph.validation: If present, must be a non-empty string equal to the composition subgraph name for this source.
subgraph.authors: Name which composed subgraph owns this annotation. Use the same subgraph name you use everywhere else for that source. Omit when a single-source schema does not need attribution.
subgraph.implementers: Attribute ownership only; do not send `subgraph` to the graph store.

value.authors: Plural form for generated list/connection fields.
value.implementers: Substitute this string for default pluralization.
